title: 1999 AHSME Problem 28
statement:
Let \(x_1,\) \(x_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(x_n\) be a sequence of integers such that

(i) \(-1 \le x_i \le 2,\) for \(i = 1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots,\) \(n\);

(ii) \(x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_n = 19;\) and

(iii) \(x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \cdots + x_n^2 = 99.\)

Let \(m\) and \(M\) be the minimal and maximal possible values of \(x_1^3 + x_2^3 + \cdots + x_n^3,\) respectively. What is \(\dfrac{M}{m}?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(a, b, c\) be the numbers of \(-1\)s, \(1\)s, and \(2\)s. Then \(-a + b + 2c = 19\) and \(a + b + 4c = 99,\) giving \(a = 40 - c\) and \(b = 59 - 3c\) with \(0 \le c \le 19.\)

The sum of cubes is \(-a + b + 8c = 19 + 6c.\) The minimum is at \(c = 0\) (value \(19\)) and the maximum at \(c = 19\) (value \(133\)), so \(\dfrac{M}{m} = \dfrac{133}{19} = 7.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let \(a, b, c\) count the \(-1\)s, \(1\)s, and \(2\)s (zeros do not matter)
The sum of cubes is \(-a + b + 8c = 19 + 6c;\) optimize over the allowed range of \(c\)
